editorialDecl.p: This transcription was produced using the online transcription editor developed by the Center for Digital Humanities at the University of Trier as part of the Workspace for Collaborative Editing Project between 2010 and 2013 and made available for use by the Institute for Textual Scholarship and Electronic Editing and the University of Birmingham.

ab.note: Not sure what is going on here. Looks like ευθεως beginning to be written then the ε was erased and the word was finished with a υς. What do you think?

This is an unclean spirit and it is also not a Nomen Sacrum
I am having trouble reading this correction. Its in the left margin
This is not a nomen sacrum. It looks like it is because the text notes that it is an unclean spirit.

Why the spaces here and in the following lines?

Scribe uses obelisk to indicate old testament quotations
there is a marginal note in the left margin that has a marking here. Likely liturgical
There is a space in this word. Why? There are a few other words before this time that also have spaces in the middle of the word. Perhaps the scribe is mimicking something in the vorlage?
another space in the middle of εισιν
Does this θς look like an addition? It does to me.

there is a large space here between these two words. Does it indicate that the scribe was even mimicking the spaces in the exemplar? It could be space intended for lectionary markings. But there are not inserted. This makes me think that the space may be something that the scribe was attempting to memick in the exemplar. Possibly making a word for word, line by line, page by page correspondence between the exemplar and his copy.
Does the overbar mean that the scribe meant this to be ηρξαντο?
This is a Family 13 Reading (correction) in the margin here.
